GC, Sep 2025: GC, Aug 2024: No further news about development of an LNG terminal in Itaqui or elsewhere in Maranhão state over the past 13 months; Gregor, July 2023: Different sources show very different capacity and cost figures for this terminal. Brazilian govt and Port of Itaqui say capacity will be 14 million cubic meters per day, Eneva says 21 million. Brazilian government estimates investment cost of 352.3 million BRL, Eneva estimates 1 billion BRL. As stipulated in the product manual, I've listed the higher capacity figure, and the median cost figure. Four competing projects for an FSRU near Itaqui port remain in play: São Marcos Bay FSRU (New Fortress Energy), Dislub Maranhão FSRU (Dislub Equador), Geramar FSRU (Gera Maranhão) and Itaqui FSRU (Eneva/Servtec). in April 2023 Itaqui's port authority received authorization to install a new FSRU berth. Next step is to solicit bids from interested developers. As of July 2023, a timeline for the bidding process had not yet been established. In July 2023, Gregor changed wiki page title from São Luis FSRU to Itaqui FSRU to reflect name most commonly used in recent media coverage.

GC, Aug 2024: Terminal began operating in late February 2024 (FSRU vessel name=Energos Celsius.) New Fortress press release reported capacity to be 6 Mtpa, compared to the previous 15 bcm/y we had listed under project details, so I've updated this figure.

GC, Aug 2025: Moving to shelved-inferred. The Nimofast website still shows a start date of 2025, yet there has been absolutely no new information about the project in the past two years. Note that I've cited Eixos above, a website that fastidiously covers Brazilian energy news, and their last article about Nimofast dates back to August 2023. I've also cited a January 2025 document from Brazil's national petroleum agency that makes it look like Nimofast may be having legal troubles / appeals denied by the courts (though it's hard to tell if this has anything to do with them abandoning the terminal project).

GC, Sep 2024: No news since 2023. Project is still described on company website as having a 2025 startup date, but this seems quite unlikely. Should be moved to Shelved in 2025 if no further developments; Gregor, July 2023: Status of this project remains uncertain. According to an interview with the company's CEO, this project combines an FSU with an onshore regas terminal. However, a different news source says that LNG from the FSU will simply be loaded onto trucks in containers and delivered to end users who will regasify it themselves. Hopefully we can get more precise details during the 2024 update.

Gregor, Sep 2025: Moved from Shelved to Cancelled; no news for >4 years

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit:
GC, Sep 2025: In April 2025, Eneva signed a Share Purchase and Sale Agreement to acquire Ceiba Energy's Jandaia power plant, along with Ceiba's proposed new Pecém FSRU project, pending fulfillment of precedent conditions and regulatory approvals. Brazil's Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) approved the sale at the end of May. I've gone ahead and added the new Pecém terminal project as a proposed unit under Eneva's ownership, and am changing status of the original Petrobras unit from idled to retired.

GC, Sep 2024: This terminal was indefinitely idled at the end of December 2023 due to the expiration of Petrobras's contract. The Pecém port authority began seeking a new operator for the terminal in 2024. In August 2024, Ceiba Energy confirmed that it would be sourcing gas for its newly announced 2.43 GW Jandaia power station from a 138,000m3 FSRU with a regasification capacity of up to 750,000 MMBtu/day, docked at the Port of Pecém. Given that the power plant was in the very early stages of development, it was not entirely clear whether Ceiba Energy's FSRU would be docked at the same berth previously used by Petrobras.

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit:
GC, Sep 2025:  It's hard to tell exactly what's going on with the construction timeline for Porto Central, the brand-new port where this terminal would be based -- and it's also hard to tell whether an LNG terminal is still in the works, or when it might begin operating. One thing that seems clear that things are moving slower than planned. One source above (GiroCapixaba) says the port project has stalled out with no measurable progress, due to competition from other port projects in nearby Rio de Janeiro state, as well as growing skepticism from investors and government officials. Another source (Portal Portuario) says that construction has been limited to preparation of a quarry that will provide rocks for the port's breakwater. A third source (IBL-Instituto Brasil Logística) says that the port will be developed in five phases, with the last not complete until 2040. As of Sep 2025, Porto Central's webpage offers no specifics, simply describing the possibility of LNG imports in general terms, as follows: "O Porto Central pode se tomar uma das principais rotas de abastecimento de gás natural para o país através de GNL importado ou do aproveitamento do gás associado offshore." Given all the uncertainty about the project's progress, and the lack of any dependable news over the past two years, I'm changing status from Proposed to Shelved.

GC, Sep 2024: Shipyard construction for the brand-new Porto Central port facility is scheduled to begin by the end of 2024, following issuance of an installation license in May 2023. The first phase of construction will focus on petroleum transfer infrastructure, while the LNG terminal will be part of a later phase, with a tentative start date of 2027. However, as of Sep 2024 there are no concrete signs of progress with the LNG terminal, so that timeline seems likely to slip.

Gregor, Sep 2025: As of July 2025, both Eneva and Macaé's municipal government continued to speak of the Tepor project in vague terms, implying that construction had not yet begun. Eneva's director of external relations Aurélio Amaral made it clear that the LNG terminal was still under consideration, noting that it would be part of a future phase of the project, but without confirming a timeline for its development.

GC, Sep 2024: Construction start date appears to have slipped into 2025, with completion expected no earlier than 2027 or 2028; Gregor, July 2024: Construction of the brand-new Tepor Macaé port complex is scheduled to begin in the first half of 2024, with commercial operations starting up as early as the end of 2026. However, the precise timeline for the LNG terminal itself remains unclear. Cost estimates appear to be for the port project as a whole, not just the LNG terminal.
